messages.subject: Delimiting contexts for data extraction
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

We are using a technique you describe in your book for extracting data from
our corpora using R; however, we've run into a problem.

The extraction using the "grep" function extracts a huge amount of context
out of our files which really clog up the excel files. Some of the contexts
are hundreds of words long. Is there any way to delimit the contexts so that
only a certain number of words before and after the target word are
extracted?

The text files of the interviews have been processed so that each line
begins a new speaker turn. The problem arises from the fact that the
interviewee in a "good" sociolinguistic interview does most of the talking,
hence few speaker turns and really LONG turns for the interviewee.

messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Delimiting contexts for data extraction
messages.body_plain:
Sali

As a relatively quick solution, have you tried using the exact.matches function that Stefan provides as part of the code accompanying his book and described on p. 141 of the book? Component [[3]] of the output from that function gives you concordance lines from the input. As it is written, the function gives the whole of the line before the matched word and the whole of the line after the matched word, using the following bit of script:

# generate a vector with lines that have tab stops before and after each match
      lines.with.delimited.matches<-paste("Line: ", line.numbers, "\t",
                                          substr(lines, 1, starts-1), "\t",
                                          substr(lines, starts, stops), "\t",
                                          substr(lines, stops+1, nchar(lines)),
                                          sep="")

You could alter the amount of text before and after the matched word by changing the arguments to something like:

# generate a vector with lines that have tab stops before and after each match
      lines.with.delimited.matches<-paste("Line: ", line.numbers, "\t",
                                          substr(lines, starts-20, starts-1), "\t",
                                          substr(lines, starts, stops), "\t",
                                          substr(lines, stops+1, stops+20),
                                          sep="")

I think this would give you something like what you are looking for, but maybe not exactly what you want.

John

messages.subject: problem saving output + encoding issues
messages.body_plain:
Hi, all.

I've been having trouble saving my outputs, and I hope you guys can
help me out. For every match, I need to press ENTER, so I assume there
must be something wrong or missing in the script I'm using:

dez.teses<-c(lp1,lp2,lp3,lp4,lp5,lp6,lp7,lp8,lp9,lp10)

mos<-unlist(strsplit(dez.teses,"\\W+"))
mos2<-gsub("(\\W)","\\1",dez.teses,perl=T)
mos3<-unlist(strsplit(mos2," ") )
(matches.in.datafile<-grep("(rmos$)",mos3,ignore.case=T))
for(i in matches.in.datafile) {
  cat(mos3[max(0,i-15):max(0,i-1)], "\t",   mos3[i],"\t",  mos3[(i
+1):min(i+10,length(mos3)+1)], file=file.choose(), append=T, "\n")}

Regarding Unicode, now that I'm running R on a Mac,  I have no idea
how to fix encoding problems. When I open the output file using
OpenOffice Calc or excel, I don't always get that wizard with the
options. When I do get it, there's no UTF-8 option.

thanks in advance!
Fernanda Canever

messages.body_plain:
Re the output issue: Well, you prompt yourself for a file (with
file.choose()) in every iteration. Do this:

output.file <- file.choose()

for(i in matches.in.datafile) {
   cat(mos3[max(0,i-15):max(0,i-1)], "\t",   mos3[i],"\t",

mos3[(i+1):min(i+10,length(mos3)+1)], "\n", file=output.file,
append=T)
}

HTH,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
